why: Kids + families: real animal facts with a fun explorer. Animal facts are one of the most watched evergreen Shorts topics, and they teach.

series.name: Wild Superpowers
series.style: 3D animated nature film look, bright natural colours, jungles, oceans, deserts and mountains, animals shown cute but true to life, sunny and exciting mood, vertical 9:16 frame
series.negative: text, letters, words, watermark, logo, gore, blood, animals hurting each other, scary, blurry

characters.name: Kiko
characters.look: Kiko, an energetic 9-year-old boy explorer with brown skin, a green safari hat, big binoculars and a khaki vest with many pockets

characters.name: Pip
characters.look: Pip, a tiny talking hummingbird with shimmering emerald-green feathers and a ruby-red throat

rules: One animal per episode. Kiko and Pip discover its real superpower and two or three true facts about it.
Only true, well-known facts, using the numbers exactly as given in the episode idea. Never invent numbers.
No gore and no animals hurting each other; hunting is only hinted at.
Start with a 'Did you know?' style hook; end by asking viewers to guess the next animal.

topics: Octopus: has three hearts and blue blood, and can change both colour and skin texture in an instant to hide.
Mantis shrimp: throws one of the fastest punches in the animal kingdom, fast enough to crack shells, and has far more colour-sensing cells in its eyes than humans.
Tardigrade (water bear): a tiny animal smaller than 1 mm that can survive freezing, boiling heat, drying out and even being sent into space.
Axolotl: a Mexican salamander that can regrow its legs, tail and even parts of its heart.
Peregrine falcon: the fastest animal on Earth, diving at over 300 km/h to catch prey in the air.
Electric eel: can make electric shocks of several hundred volts to stun fish and defend itself.
Hummingbird: the only bird that can fly backwards; its heart can beat over 1,000 times a minute.
Owl: can turn its head about 270 degrees, and its soft feathers let it fly almost silently.
Chameleon: its eyes move separately to look two ways at once, and its sticky tongue shoots out faster than you can blink.
Snow leopard: lives high in the mountains, including Pakistan's north; its thick tail helps it balance and keeps its face warm like a scarf.
Markhor: Pakistan's national animal, a wild goat with long spiral horns that climbs steep cliffs with ease.
Bat: many bats find food in total darkness using echolocation: they shout and listen to the echoes.
Dolphin: can sleep with half of its brain at a time, so one half stays alert and it can keep coming up to breathe.
Platypus: a mammal that lays eggs and can sense tiny electric signals from prey with its bill.
Indus river dolphin: lives in Pakistan's Indus river, is almost blind, and finds food using echolocation.
moreIdeas: Cheetah: the fastest land animal, reaching around 100 km/h in short bursts; its long tail helps it steer.
Elephant: its trunk has tens of thousands of muscles, and it can sense rumbles through the ground with its feet.
Camel: its hump stores fat, not water, and a thirsty camel can drink over 100 litres of water in about 10 minutes.
Archerfish: shoots jets of water from its mouth to knock insects off leaves into the water.
Ant: some ants can carry objects many times heavier than their own body and work together in huge colonies.
Firefly: makes its own cold light (bioluminescence) to talk to other fireflies.
Giraffe: has the same number of neck bones as a human, just seven, but each one is huge.
Emperor penguin: the dads keep the egg warm on their feet under a belly fold through the freezing Antarctic winter.
Gecko: can walk up walls and on ceilings thanks to millions of tiny hairs on its toes.
Sea turtle: can find its way across whole oceans, and scientists think it uses Earth's magnetic field like a compass.
Woodpecker: hammers wood many times a second without getting a headache; its long tongue wraps around its skull like a seatbelt.
Arctic tern: flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year, the longest migration of any animal, around 70,000 km.
Pistol shrimp: snaps its claw so fast it makes a bubble that pops with a loud crack, loud enough to stun small fish.
Kangaroo: a newborn joey is about the size of a jelly bean and crawls into its mother's pouch to grow.
Mudskipper: a fish that walks on mud using its fins and can breathe through its skin; it lives on Pakistan's coast too.
